comparison_project: NVIDIA Test Harness DDGI vs Path Tracer - Cornell Box indirect diffuse

candidate.name: NVIDIA RTXGI-DDGI Test Harness
candidate.random_seed: SDK volume rngSeed=12345; static volume, successive frames

reference.name: Official Test Harness Path Tracer
reference.seed: pixelIndex * frameNumber; independent run uses frameNumber + 104729

check.reliability: Independent-reference error is measured and compared with candidate error; finite-sample PT is not an exact solution.

scene.lighting: Ceiling point at (0,1.9,0), white, power=1, radius=4; sun=0, spot=0, black sky
scene.material: Official original Cornell glTF materials, no edits

camera.pixel_sampling: center (0.5,0.5), no jitter, no lens sampling

signal.name: indirect_diffuse_radiance
signal.definition: DDGI output float texture before composite; PT sum of surface direct-light estimates at bounceIndex > 0 weighted by path throughput. Black environment. Both contain primary surface albedo/BRDF. Camera-hit direct excluded.
signal.color_space: linear RGB in sample working primaries (sRGB assumed)
signal.scale: native sample radiance units, no normalization or fitted scaling

image.format: OpenEXR float32 RGB, ZIP lossless; DDGI source float16 RGBA

flip.exposure_selection: reference-only valid scene rectangle x=241..675 y=53..486; frozen for all candidate/reference checks
flip.reduction: compute full-frame error map then mean over fixed surface mask

capture.stability_assessment: Near steady: frame 32769 to 65537 HDR-FLIP drops from 0.172905 to 0.171897; mean luminance rises 0.214%. Small residual drift remains.

timing.tool: Official sample D3D12 GPU timestamp queries
timing.scope: DDGI aggregate: probe tracing, blending, relocation, classification, indirect screen query
timing.excluded: GBuffer, composite, UI, presentation, readback, CPU
timing.method: same DDGI run preceding capture, no readback checkpoints in interval

limitations: Static Cornell Box, one camera and one ceiling point light only; no dynamic stability conclusion.
Measurement patch exports linear float textures, suppresses bounce-0 direct contribution in PT, and changes only the second PT random sequence. Official DDGI SDK and DDGI shaders are unchanged.
PT uses official 20-bounce cap, maxAlbedo=0.9 and throughput termination 0.005; reference is the official finite-path model, not an infinite-bounce physical truth.
Official DDGI screen albedo is encoded in the GBuffer and decoded; PT uses hit albedo directly. The harness original color-conversion and quantization differences are preserved.
GI timing is measured over preceding steady-state frames separately from readback-heavy capture frames. Per-capture wall-clock time is unavailable.

FLIP exposure bounds are selected once from the PT visible-scene bounding rectangle; including the large black background would give a degenerate median. FLIP itself is evaluated on the full image before masking.
After 65,536 warmup frames, checkpoint HDR-FLIP still changes by about 0.001 over the last doubling. Report is a bounded long-warmup, near-steady snapshot, not proof of exact convergence.
